title: Effective particle size governs structure and dynamics in rough hard-particle fluids
authors: Nanqing Xiao, Zhen Zhang, Walter Kob, Yujie Wang
abstract: We numerically investigate how particle surface roughness affects the static and dynamic properties of a hard-particle fluid across a wide range of densities, rho. These simulations of a simple model of granular systems reveal that, although the amplitude and coverage of surface corrugation significantly influence the rho-dependence of system properties, the qualitative behavior of this dependence remains unchanged. These findings can be described quantitatively by introducing an effective particle size, which enables a direct mapping of the rough particle systems to equivalent hard-disk systems. Analytical calculations provide an explicit form of this mapping, and allow us to predict the static and dynamic properties of rough particles using standard liquid-state theories for hard disks.
summary: This work numerically and analytically investigates how surface roughness modifies the behavior of hard-particle fluids. The key finding is that the system's structural and dynamic properties can be universally described by mapping them onto an equivalent hard-disk system using an 'effective particle size.' This provides a powerful theoretical tool for simplifying complex, rough particle interactions.
main_problem: The study investigates how particle surface roughness affects the static and dynamic properties of hard-particle fluids.
main_result: The structural and dynamic properties can be mapped onto equivalent hard-disk systems using an effective particle size, demonstrating a universal scaling behavior.
method: The authors use numerical simulations and analytical calculations to derive an effective particle size and map the system's behavior onto standard liquid-state theories.
model_or_system: The system models rough hard-particle fluids in 2D, where particles have surface asperities. Interactions are modeled using a Hertzian central force, and the system's behavior is analyzed by defining an effective particle radius ($R_{eff}$) and packing fraction ($\phi_{eff}$).
key_observables: Bond-orientational order parameter ($\psi_6$), diffusion constant ($D$), Lindemann ratio ($\gamma$), and the mean contact distance ($ ar{d}$).
important_parameters: Number density ($ho$), asperity radius ($R_a$), coverage ratio ($\kappa$), and the effective packing fraction ($\phi_{eff}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system behaves as a hard-core system, allowing for a mapping to hard-disk systems, and relies on small-roughness approximations for analytical derivations.
figures_summary: Figures demonstrate the collapse of structural ($\psi_6$) and dynamic ($D$) properties onto master curves when plotted against the effective packing fraction ($\phi_{eff}$), confirming the scaling law.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the physical model and defining the effective parameters, then using structural diagnostics ($\psi_6$) to show the master-curve collapse, and finally extending this mapping to dynamic properties like the diffusion constant ($D$).
why_interesting: While focused on classical fluids, the concept of mapping complex, rough interactions onto a simpler, effective model (hard disks) is analogous to coarse-graining or effective Hamiltonians used in quantum many-body physics.
